sections.h2: Why does the inspection step set the pace of a Garden City sale?
sections.html:
A house cannot change occupants in Garden City until the city issues a certificate of occupancy, so the inspection calendar often matters more than the buyer's financing. The city is a compact Wayne County suburb of 5.87 square miles, roughly 15 miles west of downtown Detroit. A seller who books that inspection early can build the closing around it.

The notes below cover the inspection, the permit rules behind repairs, the city's housing figures, schools and services, and what follows a transfer of title.

sections.h2: How did Garden City get its layout and its name?
sections.html:
The city takes its name from the English garden city idea. Most early home sites were cut into one-acre plots so a family could grow its own fruit and vegetables. Garden City became a village within Nankin Township in June 1927 and a city six years later. Most lots today are far smaller, some only 40 by 135 feet.

The population jumped from 9,012 in 1950 to 38,017 in 1960 and peaked at 41,864 in 1970. The 2020 Census counted 27,380 residents. Local landmarks include the site of the first Kmart, which opened in 1962 and has since been demolished, and Henry Ford's honeymoon cottage, moved here from Dearborn in 1952. Downtown centers on the corner of Ford and Middlebelt Roads.

  • The 1950s and 1960s building boom produced most of the housing, so many houses are now more than 60 years old.
  • Lots as small as 40 by 135 feet leave little room for additions or large outbuildings.
  • Ford Road and Middlebelt Road are the main corridors for commuting and errands.

sections.h2: How many Garden City homes are owner-occupied, and what are they worth?
sections.html:
Garden City leans heavily toward ownership. Census Bureau estimates for 2020 to 2024 put nearly four of every five housing units in owners' hands.

The headcount fell 4.1% from the April 2020 base, so a seller should not count on a wave of newcomers. Pricing to the true condition of the house does more to speed a sale than waiting for demand.

sections.h2: How does the Garden City certificate of occupancy work for a seller?
sections.html:
Any time a property is going to be sold or has been sold, the city requires a certificate of occupancy before the new owner occupies it. The Building Department schedules the inspection, which takes place Monday through Thursday, with a morning window from 9 a.m. to noon and an afternoon window from noon to 4 p.m. The department's FAQ lists a $200 fee, payable when the inspection date is booked, and says the certificate is good for one year.

The city warns that spring and summer are the busy season, and that a seller may wait three to six weeks for an inspection. A seller who needs a fast closing should book the inspection the day the contract is signed, or earlier. The Building Department number is (734) 793-1650.

  • Book the inspection as soon as the home is listed or under contract.
  • Fix visible safety items first, since a failed inspection means a reinspection and more waiting.
  • Ask the Building Department what a December or January inspection date would mean for a closing in the same season.

sections.h2: Which repairs need a permit in Garden City?
sections.html:
A permit is good for six months, and all inspections must happen inside that window. Roof, windows, exterior doors, siding, gutters and kitchen or bathroom remodels need a building permit. Water tanks, furnaces, air conditioners and generators need mechanical permits. Service panels, circuits, fixtures and hard-wired smoke detectors need electrical permits, and sewer repairs, sinks, toilets and showers need plumbing permits. Driveways, easement walks, patios and porch caps fall under a flatwork permit.

Sheds under 200 square feet need no building permit but still need a flatwork permit for the slab. Homeowners who live in the house may pull their own permits, while anyone paying a contractor should have the contractor pull them, at the same cost. Ask the Building Department whether any open permit on the address could affect the certificate before you list.

sections.h2: What happens if the house is a rental?
sections.html:
Garden City runs a rental certification program through its Ordinance Department at the police department, reachable at (734) 793-1748. Rental certifications run three years, and the owner must recertify before the term ends. A seller who rents the house out should confirm the certification is current and tell the buyer whether tenants will stay.

A buyer who plans to keep the house as a rental should ask the Ordinance Department how a transfer affects the existing certification.

sections.h2: What do schools and city services add to a Garden City listing?
sections.html:
The Garden City School District runs four elementary schools, a middle school, Garden City High School, home of the Cougars, and Cambridge High School as its alternative program. Tipton Academy, a charter school, serves pre-kindergarten through seventh grade. St. Raphael Catholic School closed in 2016, and the former Radcliff Middle School building became a recreation center the city bought from Schoolcraft College.

Residents receive a free 95-gallon trash container from the city's refuse contractor, and curbside recycling carts can be delivered on request. Yard waste pickup runs from the first full week of April until about the middle of December, with Christmas trees collected after December 25. Buyers ask about these basics, so a short list of them helps a listing or an offer conversation.

sections.h2: What does the Michigan transfer tax cost on a Garden City sale?
sections.html:
Sellers pay Michigan's two transfer taxes, 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state on every $500 of price (MCL 207.504, 207.525). The county treasurer collects within 15 days of the deed's delivery (MCL 207.523).

At the city's median home value of $168,800, the taxes come to roughly $1,460, and the settlement statement will show the exact figure. The buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the assessor within 45 days, and taxable value resets to the state equalized value the following year (MCL 211.27a). The assessor can tell you what the new bill is likely to be.

sections.h2: When does an as-is sale make sense for a Garden City house?
sections.html:
A small, well-kept house on a standard lot can sell through a listing, though the inspection queue and the buyer's loan both add time. A house that needs repairs to pass the certificate of occupancy, an estate property, or a seller facing a short deadline often does better with an as-is purchase.

  • Choose a listing if the house is in good repair and you can wait out the inspection queue.
  • Choose an as-is buyer if the inspector is likely to list repairs you would rather not manage.
  • Ask any buyer in writing who pays the inspection fee and handles any reinspection.

Compare offers by what you keep after transfer tax, prorated taxes and credits, and put the closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Does Garden City require an inspection before a house changes hands?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a certificate of occupancy whenever a property is sold, and the new owner cannot occupy the house without it. The Building Department at (734) 793-1650 books the inspection.

faqs.q: How long should I expect to wait for the Garden City inspection?
faqs.a: The city says a seller may wait three to six weeks in spring and summer. Booking early, or aiming for a winter inspection, shortens the wait.

faqs.q: What is the fee for a Garden City certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: The city's FAQ lists $200, paid when the inspection is scheduled, for a certificate good for one year. Confirm the current amount with the Building Department.

faqs.q: Will my Garden City buyer's tax bill be higher than mine?
faqs.a: Often. The buyer's taxable value resets to the state equalized value in the calendar year after the transfer, and the buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the assessor within 45 days.

faqs.q: Can a house that fails the inspection still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, but the certificate must be issued before the new owner moves in. Some sellers make the repairs, and others sell as-is and let the buyer complete them and request the reinspection.
